purpose: Measure whether selective Product Leadership criterion improves LAB governance decisions without creating authority confusion, unnecessary process or documentary overhead.
governance_research_questions: Does Product Leadership improve prioritization and sequencing of LAB work?
Does it identify cost of delay, cost of action and premature hardening more reliably than baseline?
Does it recommend proportionate authorization scope and reversible next steps?
Does it remain inactive for mechanical or already-decided governance operations?
Does it reduce strategic error without increasing documentary overhead beyond the value created?

governance_fixtures.title: Premature infrastructure hardening
governance_fixtures.scenario: A security-hardening workstream is consuming substantial effort before the underlying capability has demonstrated functional value.

governance_fixtures.title: Overbroad execution authorization
governance_fixtures.scenario: A proposed authorization permits documentation, runtime changes, infrastructure and deployment although only one documentary correction is required.

governance_fixtures.title: Decision without success criterion
governance_fixtures.scenario: A new integration is approved in principle but has no measurable success criterion, stop rule or review date.

governance_fixtures.title: Competing project priorities
governance_fixtures.scenario: Two projects request the same limited capacity; one has a blocking customer risk and the other has a high-potential but unvalidated opportunity.

governance_fixtures.title: Technically successful experiment without decision value
governance_fixtures.scenario: An experiment passes all technical checks but does not discriminate between the competing strategic options.

governance_fixtures.title: Integration duplicates existing capability
governance_fixtures.scenario: A proposed framework overlaps substantially with an existing criterion layer and introduces new maintenance obligations.

governance_fixtures.title: Valid audit finding with excessive remediation
governance_fixtures.scenario: An audit identifies a real defect but recommends a system-wide rebuild although a bounded correction may resolve the risk.

governance_fixtures.title: Blocking pending versus attractive backlog
governance_fixtures.scenario: A blocking evidence gap competes with several visible feature and design improvements.

governance_fixtures.title: Mechanical registry update
governance_fixtures.scenario: A verified decision has already been published and only a deterministic registry pointer must be updated.

governance_fixtures.title: Exact hash verification
governance_fixtures.scenario: The task is only to verify that a known artifact hash matches the canonical manifest.

governance_fixtures.title: Simple patch overloaded with governance
governance_fixtures.scenario: A one-line documentary typo correction is proposed with a multi-stage strategy review and new governance package.

governance_fixtures.title: Mixed factual normative and execution claim
governance_fixtures.scenario: A stakeholder asks to accept an auditor conclusion, reprioritize the roadmap and immediately execute the proposed remediation.

scoring_rules: Length, vocabulary and number of frameworks are not positive signals by themselves.
A concise abstention can outperform an elaborate response when activation is not warranted.
Technical correctness does not compensate for poor priority, disproportionate authorization or authority confusion.
Governance value requires a better decision, safer sequence or lower avoidable cost.
Scorers must freeze rationales before unblinding arm identity.
